name: annotator-extension
//: The Annotator extension, a hard fork of hypothesis/browser-extension (NOTICE.md): Hypothesis's own client in the browser, against a Hypothesis service of the settings' choosing, built by upstream's Makefile into build/. Its targets share build/, so none runs beside another (`parallelism: false`).

build.//: build/: the unpacked extension, for Firefox and Zen by default, against the service on 127.0.0.1 (settings/firefox-local.json). `-c chrome` builds for Chromium. From an empty build/: make compares times to the second on macOS, so a build for one browser just after one for another would keep the other's files.

dev.//: Rebuilds build/ on every change to src/ or the client (upstream's gulp watch), for Firefox and Zen.

run.//: Run by hand: opens Zen with build/ installed as a temporary add-on, in a fresh profile web-ext throws away on exit, never the user's own. `--firefox=firefox` opens Firefox instead.

package.//: dist/annotator-extension.xpi: the extension, built again from an empty build/ (the tests write theirs there), zipped, unsigned. Release Firefox and Zen install an add-on for good only once Mozilla has signed it (`sign`).

options.command: make clean-build && make dist/annotator-extension.xpi SETTINGS_FILE=settings/firefox-local.json && echo "\nInstall $(pwd)/dist/annotator-extension.xpi from about:addons (gear menu, Install Add-on From File)."

sign.//: Run by hand, with the network and 1Password unlocked: dist/<name>-<version>.xpi, the extension signed by Mozilla, unlisted, which release Firefox and Zen install for good. addons.mozilla.org's API key and secret are 1Password references (env), which `op run` resolves for make alone, in the account OP_ACCOUNT names. Needs a version Mozilla hasn't signed before (package.json), and the extension's changes committed: the source archive it uploads alongside (SOURCE.md) is the last commit's.

options.command: make clean-build && op run -- make sign SETTINGS_FILE=settings/firefox-local.json

test.//: Upstream's unit tests (tests/), in Chromium, with vitest's browser mode.

lint.//: Mozilla's linter on the built extension, as addons.mozilla.org would run it: errors fail, upstream's client and PDF.js warn.
